title: Process control and in silico modeling strategies for enabling high density culture of human pluripotent stem cells in stirred tank bioreactors
protocol: Thaw a vial of frozen hPSCs at 37°C until only a small rest of ice is visible.
Spray the thawed vial with ethanol and place it under a flow hood.
Dilute the cell suspension in a 15 mL conical tube using DMEM/12 medium, adding a 10-fold volume relative to the cells.
Centrifuge the diluted suspension at 300 × g for 3 minutes.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 15 mL of E8 adherent medium plus 10 μM Y27632.
Remove the coating medium from one coated T75 flask.
Transfer the cell suspension into the prepared T75 flask.
Place the T-flask in an incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Incubate cells for 48 hours.
Replace the old medium with 15 mL of fresh E8 adherent medium.
Place the flask back in an incubator.
Wash cells with PBS.
Completely remove any residue of PBS.
Add 0.04 mL/cm² StemPro™ Accutase™ and incubate for 3 minutes at 37°C.
Check for cell detachment by tilting the flask.
Dilute Accutase with a 3-fold volume of DMEM/F12.
Transfer the mixture into a conical tube.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 5 mL E8 adherent medium + 10 μM Y27632.
Determine cell count with Vi-CELL XR (or manually via Trypan blue exclusion and Neubauer chamber).
Remove the coating medium from three coated T175 flasks.
Add 35 mL of E8 adherent medium + 10 μM Y27632 containing 3.5 × 10^6 cells per flask to each flask.
Incubate for 48 hours.
Replace the medium with 35 mL fresh E8 adherent medium per flask after 48 hours.
Passage the cells 72 hours post-seeding when they reach 60-80% confluence.
Wash cells with PBS, then completely remove any residue of PBS.
Add 0.04 mL/cm^2 StemPro™ Accutase™ and incubate for 3 minutes at 37°C.
Tilt the flask to support cell detachment by tilting.
Dilute Accutase with a three-fold volume of DMEM/F12, transfer into a conical tube, and centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 minutes.
Discard the supernatant, resuspend in 25 mL E8 adherent medium + 10 μM Y27632, and determine cell density with Vi-CELL XR or manually via Trypan blue exclusion and Neubauer chamber.
Incubate cells for 48 hours.
Replace old medium with 35 mL fresh E8 adherent medium per flask.
Place flasks back in incubator.
Observe cells 72 hours after seeding.
Inoculate 4 × bioreactors at 150 mL scale or 1 × bioreactor at 500 mL scale as the next major step if applicable.
Repeat steps for inoculating multiple bioreactors and/or larger scale processes while increasing T175 flasks accordingly.
Adjust seeding density into T-flasks based on cell line dependence.
Maintain cells within ∼60%–80% confluence within 72 hours suggested for passaging.
Avoid exceeding the suggested ∼60%–80% confluence and/or passing time beyond 72 hours to maintain viability after bioreactor inoculation.
Do not prolong Accutase treatment if cells are not fully detached; a three-minute treatment is optimal for detachment.
Place the bioreactor glass vessel under the flow hood.
Pipette 1 mL of Sigmacote repeatedly to the vessel wall and bottom until no liquid is left.
Allow the vessel to dry for at least 12 hours at 20°C–22°C.
Rinse the bioreactor vessel with water to remove any Sigmacote residues.
Assemble the base, feed, and waste tubing.
Ensure one end of the pump head tubing is long enough to allow placement of tube-attached bottles under the flow hood while still attached to the bioreactor.
Attach a 0.5 mm inner diameter pump head tubing for the base tubing.
Attach both a 0.5 mm and a 1.0 mm pump head tubing for the feed and waste tubing.
Place the pump head tubing into the pump heads.
Use DASware software for pump calibration.
Prime the lines with pure water.
Weigh empty conical tubes with caps.
Place tubing outlets in each conical tube.
Start dispensing at a defined flow rate.
Weigh the filled conical tubes with caps.
Insert the weight of the dispensed water into the software interface.
Note the calibration values for feed and waste lines.
Repeat steps b–e using smaller diameter pump head tubing for feed and waste lines.
Remove the pH probe from the storage solution.
Examine the pH probe’s diaphragm for damages.
Attach the probe to the cable of the bioreactor.
Rinse with water, dry with a tissue without rubbing on the diaphragm.
Place both the pH probe and the respective temperature probe into the pH 7.00 calibration buffer.
Ensure that the diaphragm is fully submerged in the buffer.
Wait for pH and temperature readings to stabilize.
Calibrate the offset.
Repeat steps b and c using pH 4.01 calibration buffer for slope calibration.
Assemble the head plate considering the schematic.
Add a piece of silicone tubing (i.d. 1.0 mm) with a Mohr pinchcock clamp, a female Luer-Lock connector and a Luer-Lock sampling valve to the sample port.
Fix connections with cable ties.
Add a piece of silicone tubing (i.d. 4.0 mm) with a vent filter to the exit port of the exhaust gas line.
Assemble a piece of small silicone tubing (i.d. 1.0 mm) with a piece of larger silicone tubing (i.d. 4.0 mm) using a hose reduction piece.
Attach a vent filter to the larger tube and connect everything to the headspace gassing port.
Fix connections with cable ties.
Attach the impeller at the lowest-possible position of the impeller shaft.
Tighten with screws in the holding sleeve.
Attach the sintered glass frit with a small piece of tubing to the dip tube.
Position the attached glass frit directly above the impeller for cell retention during perfusion.
Attach base-, feed- and waste-tubing with bottles and respective ports at the bioreactor head plate.
Ensure the longer part of the tubing is always connected to the bottle, not the head plate.
Attach a silicone tubing (i.d. 4.0 mm; o.d. 6.0 mm) with the hose nozzle at the bottom of the inoculation bottle.
Add a piece of silicone tubing (i.d. 4.0 mm) with a vent filter to the second hose nozzle at the top of the inoculation bottle.
Attach the inoculation bottle to the respective port at the bioreactor.
Cover the bottom of the bioreactor vessel with pure water for steam autoclaving and pH probe protection.
Wrap vent filters with aluminum foil to protect from humidity.
Close silicone tubing of the sampling port with a Mohr pinchcock clamp.
Autoclave the bioreactor at 120°C for 20 minutes.
Place the bioreactor vessel into the bioreactor station.
Connect the bioreactor to the overhead drive, exhaust condenser, and temperature sensor.
Supply gas through the overlay port.
Connect cables of the pH and DO probe.
Remove the water.
Replace with 100 mL of sterile PBS using an inoculation bottle.
Place base tubing in pump B, feed tubing in pump C, and waste tubing in pump D.
Fill the base bottle with 100 mL of NaHCO3.
Prime the tubing until a drop of base is seen entering the bioreactor.
Start overlay gassing with 21% O2.
Set temperature control to 37°C.
Set stirring speed to 80 rpm.
Allow DO probe to polarize for at least 6 hours.
Perform one-point slope calibration at 100% DO.
Optional: Apply gassing with pure N2 for another 6 hours followed by zero point calibration.
Click “New Workflow” in the software.
Select Control (Cell Cultivation: pH Control (CO2/base); DO Control (XO2, F)) under Default Template.
Choose the number of reactors to be used and press “open”.
Remove tick at pH Calibration and DO Calibration.
Change process name from "Manager X" to your specific process.
Select bioreactor units to be used.
Optional: Name each unit and press “Next”.
Change the settings by pressing on “Feed C”, the tab “Pump C (Sub.)” and change “V.Mode” to “Ignore”.
Repeat for “Feed D”.
Press “pH” and the tab ”pH Control”, then change the values at “Min” to “−25%” and at “Max” to “10 mL/h”.
Select the tab “Pump B (Base)” and change “V.Mode” to “Ignore”.
Copy the Script by clicking on the individual Unit, then press on “Vessel”, select the tab “Scripting”, paste the Script, adjust the volume to your specific working volume, and press “Apply”.
Place the inoculation bottle on a lower level than the bioreactor.
Transfer PBS from the bioreactor into the inoculation bottle by gravity.
Tilt the bioreactor to transfer remaining PBS.
Discard the PBS under the flow hood after detaching the inoculation bottle.
Add 110 mL of fresh E8 suspension medium for bioreactor inoculation to the inoculation bottle.
Place the inoculation bottle on a higher level than the bioreactor and let it flow by gravity into the bioreactor.
Initiate bioreactor agitation, gassing, and temperature control.
Dissociate cells from T-flasks using a 500 mL centrifugation tube.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 100 mL of fresh E8 suspension medium for bioreactor inoculation.
Determine the cell density of the resulting cell suspension using the Vi-CELL XR.
Calculate the volume of cell suspension containing 75 million cells.
Transfer the calculated volume into the bioreactor using the inoculation bottle.
Add fresh E8 suspension medium to fill up to 150 mL in the inoculation bottle and transfer it to the bioreactor for tubing flush.
Using the software interface, click on Inoculation and press Start.
Draw a first process sample at 30 minutes after inoculation.
Measure the sample directly via Vi-CELL XR to confirm the desired cell density of 0.5 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Fill the feed bottle of the bioreactor with E8 full feed medium I and II.
If a dedicated fridge is available, place the feed bottle in the fridge at 4°C.
Calculate the required volume for the first 4 days of process duration by multiplying the process scale (150) with the sum of working volumes during this time span (825 mL).
Fill the feed bottle with 825 mL of E8 full feed medium I and add an additional 2.55 L of E8 full feed medium II after 4 days.
Without cooling, deposit only 150 mL of E8 full feed medium I in the feed bottle at 20°C–22°C for the next day's feeding.
Refill the feed bottle with 150 mL of E8 full feed medium I daily based on the applied feed rate.
Prime the feed lines after filling the feed bottle.
Change from headspace gassing to submerse gassing due to high cell growth, using a lower gassing rate.
Detach the gassing from the overlay port and attach it to the submerged port in order to supply more oxygen to the culture.
Remove the cap from the bioreactor sample port and spray with 70% Ethanol.
Connect a sterile syringe to the valve, create a slight underpressure by pulling the plunger.
Open the Mohr pinchcock clamp, slowly draw 1 mL of cell suspension into the syringe and close the clamp immediately.
Discard the initial 1 mL sample from the syringe.
Draw another 2.5 mL of sample volume using the sterile syringe.
Fill the 2.5 mL sample into a well of a low attachment 6 well plate.
Clean the sample port with 70% ethanol before closing the cap.
Transfer 2 mL of the suspension sample into tubes and centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 min.
Store the supernatant at -20°C for later metabolic analysis.
Wash the obtained cell pellet carefully with 1 mL PBS.
Add 500 μL of Accutase and mix well.
Incubate for 3 min at 37°C.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend in 2 mL PBS.
Determine the cell density with Vi-CELL XR.
Use dissociated cells from the previous step at approximately 15,000 cells per well of a 96-well plate.
Triple stain pluripotency-associated surface markers SSEA-3, SSEA-4 and TRA-1-60 in 50 μL PBS/well using appropriate dilutions for each marker.
Incubate for 12 min at 20°C–22°C.
Treat approximately 15,000 cells per well with FIX&PERM® Solution A for 15 min at 20°C–22°C.
Conduct triple staining in 50 μL PBS + FIX&PERM® Solution B (1:1 ratio) using appropriate dilutions of each antibody.
Incubate for 12 min at 20°C–22°C.
Remove the cell suspension using the inoculation bottle as described in 20.
Fill the bioreactor with 200 mL of Terg-a-zyme® solution.
Set the stirring at 150 rpm.
Incubate at 37°C for at least 12 hours.
Detach all tubing from the bioreactor.
Place the detached ends into a 500 mL beaker with approximately 500 mL of distilled water.
Pump backwards into the attached feed-, waste- and base- bottles for 2 hours.
Detach the tubes from the bottles.
Place the other end of the tubes into the distilled water-filled beaker to pump in circles for at least 12 hours.
Rinse all bioreactor ports with Terg-a-zyme® solution.
Thoroughly rinse the cell retention filter to avoid future clogging.
On the next day, remove the Terg-a-zyme® solution from the bioreactor.
Replace with distilled water.
Rinse the ports with distilled water and incubate for 4 hours.
Remove tubes from the beaker.
Continue to pump for 30 minutes to remove liquid residues from tubes.
Unscrew DO and pH sensors from the head plate.
Place the pH sensor back into the storage solution.
Remove the water from the bioreactor vessel.
Pat dry.
